findings.title: CRON cancellation query does not filter by method, so SMS reminders are also picked up and 'cancelled' via SendGrid
findings.body: The new query `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, "hour") } } })` selects ALL cancelled reminders regardless of `method`. For SMS reminders, `referenceId` is a Twilio message SID, not a SendGrid batch_id, so the subsequent `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId` will either fail or, worse, attempt to cancel an unrelated SendGrid batch if a SID collides with a batch id. The query must include `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` (and ideally `scheduled: true` / `referenceId: { not: null }`), otherwise SMS reminders marked cancelled are never actually cancelled in Twilio and are deleted from the DB by this job, leaving the scheduled SMS to still be delivered.

findings.body: The `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop awaits `client.request(...)` inside a single `try/catch` that wraps the entire loop. If the SendGrid call for the first reminder throws (network error, invalid batch_id, expired batch), the catch swallows it and the loop exits, so no further reminders are cancelled and none of the `workflowReminder.delete` promises (collected in `workflowRemindersToDelete`) are awaited. Cancelled reminders whose scheduled date is within the hour will then remain in the DB with `cancelled: true` and, because the earlier `deleteMany` only removes reminders with `scheduledDate <= now`, they can be re-processed on the next run — but more importantly, reminders later in the list never get their SendGrid scheduled send cancelled, so the emails are still sent. Each reminder's cancellation should be individually try/caught, and the DB delete should only happen after a successful SendGrid cancel (or be retried).

Deleting the DB row removes the only record that the email still needs to be cancelled, so if the SendGrid request silently fails or the row had no referenceId, the scheduled email will be sent and there is no longer any state to retry the cancellation. The delete should only occur after a successful provider cancellation, and rows without a referenceId should be handled explicitly.

findings.title: Sender ID input is now rendered for EMAIL actions, allowing users to set an SMS sender ID on email steps
findings.body: The refactor changed the wrapper condition from `{(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) && (...)}` to a separate `isPhoneNumberNeeded` block plus an unconditional `<div className="mt-2 rounded-md bg-gray-50 p-4 pt-0">` that renders either the Sender ID input (when `isSenderIdNeeded`) or the Sender Name input. `isSenderIdNeeded` is initialized to `true` when `step?.action === SMS_NUMBER || step?.action === SMS_ATTENDEE`, but it is only ever set to `false` in the action `onChange` handler — for an existing EMAIL step loaded from the DB, `isSenderIdNeeded` stays `false`, so this is mostly fine; however the sender block is now always rendered even for actions where neither sender ID nor sender name is relevant, and the `isSenderIdNeeded` state is not re-synced when `step` changes (component reuse across steps), so switching between steps in the UI can show the wrong sender field. This is a UI-state regression introduced by the restructuring; the sender block should be gated on `isSenderIdNeeded || !isEmailSubjectNeeded` (or equivalent) and the state should be derived from the current action.
